# read-api-route-budgets.txt — issue #6797: per-route p95 latency budgets for
# the backend-backed read-API latency gate.
#
# go/cmd/read-api-latency-gate seeds a synthetic corpus (ingestion scopes,
# generations, and fact_work_items across every collector kind, plus
# infra-labeled graph nodes and IaC content_entity facts) into a live
# Postgres+NornicDB pair, sweeps every no-arg GET route the generated surface
# inventory reports, and fails when a route's p95 exceeds its budget here.
#
# Format: route<TAB>budget_ms<TAB>reason. "default" (required, no reason
# column) is the budget for any route this table does not name explicitly, so
# a newly added no-arg GET route is budgeted automatically instead of going
# unchecked. Every other row requires a reason: why this route needs its own
# number instead of the default. A route named more than once is a hard
# error — a later row must never silently override an earlier one.
#
# budget.go additionally consults the capability catalog
# (go/internal/capabilitycatalog): for a route RouteCapability maps to a
# capability with a declared production p95_latency_ms, the effective budget
# is min(catalog_p95 * 1.5, this table's value) — the catalog value only ever
# TIGHTENS the row below, never loosens it silently. See budget.go's
# catalogCIMultiplier doc comment for why 1.5x.
#
# Provenance: the #6793/#6794 family budgets below are post-fix targets set
# by issue #6797's own acceptance criteria, not what the gate measures on
# unpatched main — those routes are expected to breach until the underlying
# regressions are fixed:
#   - #6793 (infra resource aggregate / IaC inventory full-scan cost).
#   - #6794 (status/readiness routes paying per-scope activeFactWorkItemsCTE
#     cost).
#
# ACCEPTED KNOWN GAP: infra/resources/count and infra/resources/inventory
# ARE budgeted and exercised by this gate, but they are NOT
# regression-sensitive at CI seed scale — reviewed and accepted, not an
# oversight. At the largest seeded graph volume this gate's CI time budget
# can afford (150k synthetic nodes per infra label, 1.2M total), both
# measured well under 100ms — the seeded graph scan never got close to the
# 10s graph-read timeout (query/neo4j_read_policy.go) that produces #6793's
# live failures. That live slowness depends on NornicDB's actual load and
# cache state at production scale, which a CI-bounded synthetic seed cannot
# reproduce; calibrating further is not planned. iac/resources (a DIFFERENT
# #6793 sub-mechanism, the Postgres jsonb-detoast cost in
# currentInventoryCTE) DID reproduce and scales as expected with seeded row
# count.

default	1500

# Borderline family: single-domain reducer-fact aggregates that sit close to
# a 1s read budget at this gate's seeded scale.
GET /api/v0/freshness/generations	2000	borderline family: near the default budget at seeded scale
GET /api/v0/supply-chain/container-images/identities/count	2000	borderline family: near the default budget at seeded scale
GET /api/v0/supply-chain/impact/findings/count	2000	borderline family: near the default budget at seeded scale
GET /api/v0/graph/entities	2000	borderline family: near the default budget at seeded scale

# #6793 family: infra resource aggregate / IaC inventory. Post-fix target
# 2000ms (issue #6797 acceptance). infra/resources/{count,inventory} map to
# platform_impact.infra_resource_aggregate (catalog production p95=2500ms,
# looser than this target, so this row wins per budget.go's tighter-wins
# rule); iac/resources maps to iac_inventory.resources.list (catalog
# production p95=3000ms, likewise looser).
GET /api/v0/infra/resources/count	2000	#6793 post-fix target; catalog p95 2500ms is looser; ACCEPTED KNOWN GAP, see header
GET /api/v0/infra/resources/inventory	2000	#6793 post-fix target; catalog p95 2500ms is looser; ACCEPTED KNOWN GAP, see header
GET /api/v0/iac/resources	2000	#6793 post-fix target; catalog p95 3000ms is looser; reproduces at seeded IaC fact scale

# #6794 family: status/readiness/multi-scope routes paying activeFactWorkItemsCTE
# and large intent-table scan cost. Post-fix target 1000ms (issue #6797
# acceptance). status/operations maps to operations.status (catalog
# production p95=2000ms, looser than this target, so this row wins); the
# rest have no mapped capability in RouteCapability (see budget.go's doc
# comment on why an exhaustive mapping isn't derivable).
GET /api/v0/collectors	1000	#6794 post-fix target
GET /api/v0/collector-readiness	1000	#6794 post-fix target
GET /api/v0/status/collector-readiness	1000	#6794 post-fix target
GET /api/v0/status/collectors	1000	#6794 post-fix target
GET /api/v0/status/freshness-causality	1000	#6794 post-fix target
GET /api/v0/status/governance	1000	#6794 post-fix target
GET /api/v0/status/hosted-readiness	1000	#6794 post-fix target
GET /api/v0/status/index	1000	#6794 post-fix target
GET /api/v0/status/ingesters	1000	#6794 post-fix target
GET /api/v0/status/operations	1000	#6794 post-fix target; catalog p95 2000ms is looser
GET /api/v0/status/operator-control-plane	1000	#6794 post-fix target
GET /api/v0/status/pipeline	1000	#6794 post-fix target
GET /api/v0/status/semantic-extraction	1000	#6794 post-fix target
GET /api/v0/index-status	1000	#6794 post-fix target
GET /api/v0/ingesters	1000	#6794 post-fix target
GET /api/v0/evidence/bundle	1000	#6794 post-fix target; same activeFactWorkItemsCTE-adjacent shape
GET /api/v0/repositories	1000	#6794 post-fix target
GET /api/v0/repositories/language-inventory	1000	#6794 post-fix target

# GET /api/v0/capabilities is not part of either regression family; its row
# exists to exercise (and test-prove, see budget_test.go
# TestCatalogBudgetWinsWhenTighter) the catalog-tighter-wins path: catalog
# production p95=400ms * 1.5 = 600ms, tighter than the 1500ms default.
GET /api/v0/capabilities	1500	catalog p95 400ms*1.5=600ms is tighter and wins at runtime; row exists so this route is not silently unbudgeted if the catalog entry is ever removed
